title: Document Upload & Analysis for Ideation Sessions

summary.goal: Enable users to upload text/markdown documents when creating ideation sessions. Documents are another form of input (like chat messages) that agents analyze and distill into unified understanding. The value of ideation is the interpretation layer - transforming raw input into understanding formatted for planners.
in_scope: Document upload at session creation (text, markdown files)
Chunked document processing for large files
Analysis produces observations in UNIFIED understanding (same schema as chat-derived insights)
Source citations as metadata on any observation (not separate namespace)
Keyword/topic tagging of chunks for retrieval
Agent tool to query raw chunks by topic/keyword
out_of_scope: PDF, Word, or binary document formats (v2)
constraints: Must handle documents up to 500KB each, up to 10 documents per session
Total document content per session capped at 2MB
Chunk size ~4000 tokens to fit analyst context windows
Analysis must complete within 2 minutes for typical document sets
Must work in mock mode without API keys

acceptance_criteria.description: User can upload .txt and .md files when creating a session
Documents are stored as raw input (separate storage, like chat messages are separate from understanding)
Large documents (>4000 tokens) are automatically chunked
Each chunk is tagged with topics/keywords during analysis
Analysis produces observations in UNIFIED understanding schema (not separate namespace)
Channel receives summary message with topic index when analysis completes
Agents have a tool to query raw chunks by topic/keyword
Observations can include optional source citation (e.g., source: 'doc:requirements.md:L10-20')
Session shows analysis status: pending | analyzing | ready | failed
Understanding contains interpreted insights - never raw document text

decisions.decision: All input (chat + documents) distills into UNIFIED understanding
decisions.rationale: Documents are just another information source. There's no 'document understanding' vs 'chat understanding' - agents synthesize ALL input into one understanding schema that helps planners plan.

decisions.decision: Source citations as metadata, not separate namespace
decisions.rationale: An observation like 'auth must use OAuth2' can have source: 'doc:requirements.md:L15' or source: 'chat:turn-3'. No Understanding.document_insights - just Understanding.{specialist}.observations with optional source.

decisions.decision: Documents are raw input storage (like transcript)
decisions.rationale: Just as chat messages are stored as transcript but understanding is separate, documents are stored raw but understanding contains only interpreted insights.
Simpler, no embedding API dependency, no vector store. Topics/keywords extracted during analysis enable targeted retrieval without semantic search complexity.
All agents see what topics are available. Format: 'Analyzed 3 docs. Topics: auth, scaling, data-model. Query with cite_document(topic) tool.'
Allows handling large documents. Analysis runs on upload so session starts ready.
Spawn for analysis, exit when done. No need for persistent services.

observations: Input layer (raw storage): transcript (chat) + documents (files) - stored separately
Output layer: unified Understanding schema - agents synthesize ALL input here
Analysis flow: Upload → Chunk → Tag → Synthesize into Understanding → Ready
Agent tool: cite_document(topic) returns raw chunk for precise quoting
Source citations are metadata on observations, e.g., { observation: '...', source: 'doc:req.md:L10' }
Channel integration: Post summary with topic index when analysis completes
questions: Should topic extraction use LLM or simpler NLP?
How to handle chunks that span multiple topics?
concerns: Rate limiting with parallel chunk analysis

observations: Document (raw storage): id, session_id, filename, content, mime_type, size, status, topics[]
DocumentChunk (raw storage): id, document_id, index, content, start_line, end_line, topics[], keywords[]
Session.documents: references to attached documents (raw input, like Session.transcript)
Understanding (unified): Record<specialist, { observations: Observation[] }> where Observation can have optional 'source' field
Example observation with source: { text: 'OAuth2 required', source: 'doc:requirements.md:L15-20', confidence: 'high' }
NO separate Understanding.document_insights namespace - all insights go to appropriate specialist
Interviewer's context includes understanding summary (already unified)
Interviewer has cite_document tool to retrieve raw sections when needed
When spawning specialists, include relevant document topics in their context
Specialists add to unified understanding - with source citations when from docs

tool_design.name: cite_document
tool_design.description: Retrieve raw document sections by topic or keyword for precise quoting

observations: Ideation's value = interpretation layer between raw input and planners
If we just forwarded docs to planner, why have ideation?
Agents distill ALL input (chat + docs) into understanding formatted for planners
This must be central to agent prompts - they understand this is their task

architect.storage: SQLite - documents table + chunks table with JSONB for tags (raw input layer)
architect.understanding: Existing Understanding schema unchanged - observations gain optional 'source' metadata
architect.chunking: Token-based splitting (~4000 tokens) with ~100 token overlap
architect.tagging: LLM extracts 3-7 topic tags per chunk during analysis
architect.parallelism: Max 3 concurrent chunk analyses to respect rate limits

observation_with_source.note: Source is optional. Chat-derived observations may omit source or use 'chat:turn-N'.

channel_message_format.example:
📄 Analyzed 3 documents (requirements.md, architecture.md, constraints.txt).

Topics found: authentication, data-model, scaling, api-design, security

Use cite_document('topic') to reference specific sections.
